chief_data.selection_justification: Candidate 1 (τ=0.6 min, Q=0.5 mL/min) is selected as the first screen experiment. It achieves a 5× residence-time reduction relative to the 3-min batch benchmark, approaching the 6× intensification hypothesis, while operating at the higher end of the pump's practical range (0.5 mL/min vs 0.4 mL/min for candidate 2). The researcher objective is a practical first flow experiment using only available equipment; candidate 1 provides a slightly more productive starting point (1867 mg/h proxy vs 1499 mg/h) and a wider ±30% operating envelope (Q: 0.35–0.65 mL/min) that accommodates lab variability without hitting the pump minimum floor. Both candidates are feasible screens; candidate 1 is preferred because its higher Q gives more headroom above the 0.1 mL/min pump minimum and its envelope fully spans the runner-up's center point, meaning a single screen at candidate 1 conditions implicitly brackets candidate 2 as well. The proposed flow advantage (hazardous-intermediate holdup reduction and productivity gain) is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated result; this is a SCREEN disposition.
chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 1 (combined score 0.807) edges candidate 2 (0.793) by 1.8%, within the 5% tiebreak band, so tiebreak criteria apply. Both candidates are identical in safety (1.000), geometry (1.000), and PVS (0.672); candidate 1 leads in chemistry (0.820 vs 0.760), kinetics (0.720 vs 0.680), and fluidics (0.820 vs 0.780), reflecting its slightly higher throughput and better alignment with the intensification screening objective. The researcher objective is a practical first flow experiment, not a demonstrated optimum; candidate 1 at Q=0.5 mL/min and τ=0.6 min is selected because its ±30% design envelope (Q: 0.35–0.65 mL/min, τ: 0.42–0.78 min) fully contains candidate 2's center point (Q=0.4 mL/min, τ=0.75 min), meaning a single run at candidate 1 conditions with a subsequent flow-rate screen naturally traverses both candidates' operating space. The most important remaining uncertainties are: (1) actual liquid holdup and true contact-time in the Cu/C CatCart packed bed — the 0.3 mL geometric volume is an upper bound on residence time, and bed voidage (unknown) will reduce effective τ; and (2) Cu leaching from the CatCart into the acetone product stream, which must be quantified by ICP-MS before any pharmaceutical application. The first bench experiment should verify that the system reaches steady state (confirmed by stable back-pressure and outlet concentration) within 3–5 reactor volumes (~1.5–2.5 min at 0.5 mL/min), then collect a sample for HPLC conversion analysis and ICP-MS Cu content; conversion and pressure drop are the primary go/no-go readouts. All conversion and productivity figures are unvalidated screening proxies derived from batch analogy kinetics and empty-tube hydraulic models that do not apply to this packed bed.
resolved_tradeoffs: id=1 vs id=2: scores within 5% tiebreak band (1.8% gap); tiebreak applied. Safety and geometry scores are identical (1.000/1.000). Candidate 1 leads in chemistry, kinetics, and fluidics domains.

id=1 design envelope (Q: 0.35–0.65 mL/min, τ: 0.42–0.78 min) fully contains id=2 center point (Q=0.4 mL/min, τ=0.75 min); a flow-rate screen from candidate 1 conditions traverses both candidates' space in a single experimental series.
id=1 Q=0.5 mL/min provides more headroom above pump minimum (0.1 mL/min) than id=2 Q=0.4 mL/min; both are well within the 0.1–3.0 mL/min pump range.

BPR constraint is identical for both: only available setpoint is 20 bar (bpr_xcube_20). Acetone vapour pressure at 150°C ≈ 11.3–11.8 bar; 20 bar BPR provides ≥8 bar margin above the hard minimum of 11.81 bar confirmed by both envelope computations. This is the only available BPR and it is mandatory.
Reactor geometry is fixed (reactor_cuc_cart_030, 0.3 mL, 4 mm ID, SS): no geometry tradeoff exists between candidates. Both use identical hardware.
Empty-tube hydraulic model is not applicable to this packed bed; ΔP=0.0 bar is a placeholder, not a measurement. Actual bed pressure drop is unknown and must be measured on first run.

r_mix values (111 for id=1, 89 for id=2) are empty-tube diffusion proxies inapplicable to packed-bed transport; they are not used as disqualifying criteria here because the packed bed provides its own mixing enhancement.

overridden_concerns.concern: r_mix=111 (id=1) and r_mix=89 (id=2) are elevated, indicating diffusion-limited mixing in empty-tube model
overridden_concerns.override_reason: The mixing model is explicitly flagged as not applicable to this packed-bed reactor (model_validity.mixing.applicable=false). The Cu/C CatCart packed bed provides interstitial convection and surface contact that the empty-tube diffusion proxy does not capture. Da_mass=2456 is similarly an empty-tube artefact. These values are not valid disqualification criteria for a packed-bed system.

remaining_uncertainties: Actual liquid holdup and true contact time in the Cu/C CatCart: bed voidage, particle size, and packing density are unknown. The geometric V_R=0.3 mL is an upper bound; effective residence time may be significantly shorter. This is the primary kinetic uncertainty.
Cu leaching from the CatCart into the acetone product stream: must be quantified by ICP-MS on the first collected fraction before any downstream use or scale-up.
Actual packed-bed pressure drop at 0.5 mL/min and 150°C is unknown; the ΔP=0.0 bar placeholder must be replaced by measurement on the first run.

Axial dispersion in the 4 mm ID CatCart is significant (Péclet number estimated ~4 for empty tube; packed bed may be worse or better depending on particle size). RTD characterisation with a tracer pulse is recommended after the first conversion screen.
Kinetic transfer from microwave batch (150°C, 3 min, homogeneous Cu/C suspension) to continuous packed-bed flow (heterogeneous Cu surface, unknown wetting) is assumed but not demonstrated.
chief_data.experiment_recommendation: SETUP: Install reactor_cuc_cart_030 (Cu/C CatCart, 0.3 mL, 4 mm ID) in the X-Cube cartridge holder behind the blast shield (safety_cuaac_shield). Set heater_xcube to 150°C and bpr_xcube_20 to 20 bar. FEED PREPARATION: Prepare a single premixed feed solution of benzyl azide (0.25 M) and phenylacetylene (0.275 M, 1.1 equiv) in acetone in an amber vial behind the blast shield; prepare at ambient temperature immediately before use. PRIMING: Prime the system with neat acetone at Q=0.5 mL/min at ambient temperature and 20 bar BPR until steady back-pressure is confirmed (≥5 reactor volumes, ~3 min). HEAT-UP: Ramp heater to 150°C with acetone flowing; allow 5 min for thermal equilibration. REACTION: Switch feed to the premixed substrate solution at Q=0.5 mL/min (pump_xcube_hplc). Collect and discard the first 5 reactor volumes (~3 mL, ~6 min) as transient material. Collect steady-state fraction (~2 mL) in collector_amber_100. ANALYSIS: Analyse by HPLC for conversion and yield of 1-benzyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3-triazole; submit aliquot for ICP-MS Cu analysis. Record actual system pressure (pump head pressure minus BPR setpoint = ΔP_bed). FLOW-RATE SCREEN (if first point succeeds): Repeat at Q=0.3, 0.4, 0.7, 1.0 mL/min (τ_nominal=1.0, 0.75, 0.43, 0.3 min) to map conversion vs residence time. SAFETY NOTES: Benzyl azide is a primary organic azide — shock and heat sensitive at high concentration. Maintain 0.25 M maximum concentration. All operations behind blast shield. Do not heat undiluted azide. Monitor for unexpected pressure excursions; abort if pump pressure exceeds 35 bar.

final_consensus.X_estimated_note: Unvalidated screening proxy from batch-analogy first-order kinetics with IF=10×; not a measured flow conversion. Must be verified experimentally.
final_consensus.productivity_note: Proxy figure derived from unvalidated X_estimated; not a demonstrated throughput.
final_consensus.residence_time_basis: Nominal empty-bed liquid space time: V_R_geometric / Q_liquid = 0.3 mL / 0.5 mL/min = 0.6 min. Actual contact time will be shorter due to bed voidage (unknown); this is an upper bound.
final_consensus.gas_phase_note: No gas phase. Pure liquid-phase reaction. No inlet/STP gas flow. No in-channel gas flow. Gas-flow distinction is not applicable to this design.
final_consensus.pressure_note: BPR fixed at 20 bar (only available setpoint). Acetone vapour pressure at 150°C ≈ 11.3–11.8 bar; 20 bar provides ≥8.2 bar margin. Absolute reactor pressure ≈ 20 + 1.013 = 21.0 bar. Packed-bed ΔP is unknown (placeholder 0.0 bar); must be measured on first run. Pump maximum is 40 bar; total system pressure budget is adequate.

pump_flowrates.role: single combined substrate feed (benzyl azide + phenylacetylene in acetone)
pump_flowrates.derivation: Feed rate is set by the residence-time / reactor-volume constraint, not by a batch-productivity heuristic. Q = V_R / τ = 0.3 mL / 0.6 min = 0.5 mL/min. This is the total liquid flow through the single-pump, single-stream system. Molar delivery check: ṅ_benzyl_azide = Q × C_azide = 0.5 mL/min × 0.25 mmol/mL = 0.125 mmol/min (limiting component). ṅ_phenylacetylene = 0.5 mL/min × 0.275 mmol/mL = 0.1375 mmol/min (1.1 equiv, excess). Both substrates are premixed in the single feed vial; no separate pump is required or available for a second liquid stream.
